clue.text: Tense whilst being given instructions, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that a word is said out loud and a different spelling is written

parts.note: someone being given instructions is being taught

explanation.surface: Someone grows nervous while a teacher hands out orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst' is a link word; TAUGHT and TAUT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean stretched tight, whether a rope or a nervous person's mood.

clue.text: Having lost interest, left main road

explanation.surface: A bored driver pulls off the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bored person has lost all enthusiasm, and a driver who quits a highway for a side road has done exactly that manoeuvre.

clue.text: 50% more able. How annoying

explanation.surface: Someone half again as capable proves irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: cleverer by a half. The second is the everyday sense of irritating smartness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes cleverness that tips into irritating showing off, while literally it says ability increased by a half.

clue.text: Propose place for hospital room

parts.note: to place something is to put it
taken as written
a ward is a room of beds in a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a location for a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest an idea or a candidate for consideration, as in a motion at a meeting.

clue.text: Pepper, beer and duck taken round middle east

indicators.note: taken round says the first pieces are wrapped about the next one

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A recipe in which beer and duck are cooked around something from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: PINT and O together are opened to take ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimento is a sweet red capsicum, the kind stuffed into olives.

clue.text: Jack's a cad, he comes from one of the eastern states

definitions.text: he comes from one of the eastern states

parts.note: Jack and tar are both old words for a sailor; the 's is 'is'
a heel is a contemptible, dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A sailor, a bounder, hails from America's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tar Heel is a native of North Carolina, an eastern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar Heel is the nickname for a native of North Carolina, on the US Atlantic seaboard.

clue.text: Deliver from amount carried on one trip

parts.note: off means from, as in taking a book off a shelf
a load is what a vehicle carries at one time

explanation.surface: A courier unloads a single trip's cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload goods is to hand them over at their destination; also to get rid of something.

clue.text: Deadly question for a drinker

parts.note: the barman's jokey way of asking what someone will drink, which read literally asks which lethal substance they prefer

explanation.surface: A barman asks a customer what they want, in alarming terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular pub greeting asking which drink someone would like, poison being slang for alcohol.

clue.text: The same again, endlessly affluent Greek style

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same again

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: affluent means rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy person repeats an order in a Greek architectural fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the plainest of the classical orders of Greek architecture.

clue.text: Restorer, he leaves here late

indicators.note: leaves says one word departs from the other, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A restorer who works late is the last to leave the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he leaves here' takes HE out of HERE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformer puts things right, bringing an institution back to good order.

clue.text: One completes the picture for criminal conspirator

explanation.surface: A crook is the finishing touch to a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mounts a picture in its border finishes it; one who fabricates evidence against an innocent person sets them up.

clue.text: One or two ladies, say, or sometimes a man

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name
Lyn is another woman's name

explanation.surface: A name that may belong to a woman, or two women, or occasionally a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or' and 'say' are links: the name is one lady's, or two ladies' names joined, and also a man's, as for the novelist Evelyn Waugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to both sexes; the writer Waugh was a male example.

clue.text: Say is to do with the ear going round or to do with oneself

parts.note: eg, for example, is the crossword sense of say

indicators.note: going round says one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: otic is the adjective for the ear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jumble of definitions about hearing and the self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts the ear adjective around 'is', making OISTIC; the surface hides that 'Say' gives letters rather than introducing speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred, concerned chiefly with one's own interests.

clue.text: Box that is cold inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A container keeps its contents chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is a loose definition, ice standing for the cold store or icebox.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox, often just called the ice, is the chilled chest that keeps food cold.

clue.text: I love smearing lubricant, cooking fat!

indicators.note: smearing suggests spreading things messily, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love of smearing on grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smearing' rearranges I LOVE into OLIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pressed juice of the fruit of the Mediterranean tree, used for frying and dressings.

clue.text: One drives right into port

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone drives straight into a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One drives' looks like a motorist, but means a herdsman driving cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover herds livestock along roads to market.

clue.text: Alternatively turning up at one cathedral or another

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: or means alternatively
Chester is an English cathedral city

explanation.surface: A tourist visits one cathedral, or perhaps another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' and 'or' are links; Rochester in Kent is another cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent is a second English city with a cathedral.

clue.text: Inside prefab, rich material

indicators.note: Inside says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Inside a prefabricated building there is expensive cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, the stuff garments are made of.

clue.text: Be unwell as a result of drink, it is reported

indicators.note: it is reported says what follows is heard, not read

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be poorly after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a result of' is a link; ALE and AIL sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ill or suffer from sickness.

clue.text: Hat from fellow going on the water in France

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A man's hat floats on a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on' is a link: in a down clue EAU goes below CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for a headpiece, used jokily in English.

clue.text: A Parisian coheir suffered not being courageous

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: suffered suggests being knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French co-heir endured hardship without bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' rearranges COHEIR into HEROIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking bravery, the opposite of valiant.

clue.text: Duel can result in being undone

indicators.note: result in says the letters lead to something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A fight could leave someone ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; 'Duel can result in' turns DUELCAN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes or a corset with strings untied are loosened, not fastened.

clue.text: Save him

explanation.surface: A plea to rescue a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To save is to conserve resources carefully; him read as a woman's spouse.

clue.text: Cooperate on sports field

explanation.surface: A request to work together on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with someone, and the umpire's call that starts a baseball game.

clue.text: Peter's alarm?

parts.note: the boy who never grew up has a famous surname, and adding a suffix gives a word for sudden fear

explanation.surface: A fright felt by someone called Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pan's surname plus -IC, as if 'of Pan', gives a word for terror; the word in fact comes from the god Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear, named after the god Pan who was said to cause it.

clue.text: Despite being holey it holds water

definitions.text: Despite being holey it holds water

parts.words: Despite being holey it holds water
parts.note: a thing full of holes that still soaks up liquid, the paradox of a bath item

explanation.surface: A riddle about a full-of-holes object that keeps liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous bath item that absorbs liquid in its holes.

clue.text: It isn't the goddess who'll write the music

parts.note: isn't is not
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone insists it is not a deity who will compose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' and 'who'll' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down in written notation, as a composer puts a tune on staves.

clue.text: Roughest coasters have been replaced

indicators.note: have been replaced says the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: The roughest drinks mats have been swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: COASTERS rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Most coarse, the superlative of rough or crude.

clue.text: Damned perplexed

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned oath meaning cursed, and also meaning bewildered or puzzled.

clue.text: At no time disheartened by poets

definitions.text: At no time disheartened by poets

indicators.note: disheartened says the word loses its central letter

parts.note: at no time means never

explanation.surface: Poets are never downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes V, the heart of NEVER, out; the shortened form with an apostrophe is used by poets.
explanation.definitionFit: The contracted form of never used in verse to save a syllable.
